title: Weak reducibility for bridge trisections
summary: A bridge splitting of a knot is weakly reducible if it has a pair of disjoint shadows, one from above and one from below, in the splitting surface. The process of weak reduction exchanges local minima and maxima in the splitting, untelescoping the splitting and giving a method for detecting essential surfaces in the knot complement. Bridge trisections generalize bridge splittings to the setting of surfaces in 4-manifolds.
